text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT (PAGING) — Service: /v1/generate (streaming) | Severity: P1 | Symptom: p99 tail latency spike and streaming stalls detected. p95 ~ 300ms over baseline, p99 ~ 2.8s over SLO. Affects ~12% of requests over last 5m. Paging @oncall-eng @eng-runtime @eng-ml @eng-sre

Avery: acked. I'm on it. grabbing baseline dashboards now.

Avery: quick snapshot — rolling quantization/precision profile (int8 calibration) was pushed to canary pool ~12:15 UTC. Spike starts ~12:22 UTC and tracks canary region.

Rina: confirming, we pushed a small int8 calibration tweak for long-context batching to reduce memory. Canary = pool-canary-eu-west.

Diego: logs show repeated stall messages from runtime: 
```
2026-03-14T12:22:34Z runtime.warn kv-cache-miss stream-stall seq=0x7f4a
2026-03-14T12:22:34Z runtime.error dequantize-fallback latency=1823ms model=redwood-llama-70b-int8
```

Maya: seen clients reporting incomplete streams and reconnects, frontend retries spiking. CS queue getting two escalations. Lia, can you confirm customer impact?

Lia: customers A and B reported streaming interruptions for ~30s each. Not widespread but high severity for both (real-time transcription). Filing support notes now.

Avery: hypothesis: int8 calibration change introduced a slow dequant/fallback path for some KV cache patterns causing per-request tail blowup. p95 increase likely from more frequent fallback on long context.

Diego: I can reproduce locally by replaying canary traces with the new quant profile. When a particular attention block hits, dequant path serializes and stalls streaming threads.

Rina: rollback to previous calibration on canary is low-risk. Do we want to stop the rollout entirely and fallback to fp16 for canary?

Avery: mitigation plan: 1) abort calibration rollout (deploy-bot revert request), 2) temporarily disable int8 kernel fallback path for streaming endpoints, 3) scale up streaming workers to drain backlog. Step 2 might reduce accuracy but restores latency.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated: revert-deploy 2026-03-14T12:25 UTC -> target: pool-canary-eu-west.

Chris: scaling streaming-workers +2x on canary pool now. Command: `./ops/scale --pool pool-canary-eu-west --component streamer --delta +2`

Avery: applying runtime config patch to disable int8 dequant fallback for streaming routes: `runtime.feature.toggle.disable_dequant_fallback=streaming:true` — pushing to canary only.

Diego: patch applied. Restarting streamer processes one at a time. Logs show fewer dequant errors immediately.

Avery: monitoring p95/p99 now — dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/streams/latency?var-pool=canary-eu-west

~3m later~

incident-bot: ALERT update — p99 dropped from +2.8s to +310ms above baseline in canary, request error rate unchanged. Global traffic still routing to stable unaffected.

Maya: front-end retries dropping and customer reconnect reports reduced. Lia please update customers A/B.

Lia: Notified both customers. They're verifying. CS escalation de-escalated to high -> monitor.

Rina: Canary rollback completed — deploy-bot: revert successful. We'll halt the int8 calibration rollout until root cause analysis.

Avery: decision: rollback accepted, keep runtime toggle to avoid fallback for streaming for the moment (preserve p99). We'll run a targeted test to understand which KV pattern triggers dequant path. Diego to own repro, Rina to own calibration rollback and fixes.

Diego: repro notes added to the incident thread. Key tracer: `kv.seq.len>1024` + mixed-batch streaming request triggers serialization. Working on a patch to make dequant path async.

Chris: leaving increased streamer capacity in canary for next 2 hours, then gradually reduce if stable. I'll also run a small traffic-shift to 10% canary -> stable to validate no spillover.

Maya: handoff to night SRE @Chris at 13:15 UTC (in 30m) for monitoring. I'll stay available for customer comms.

Chris: acked. Oncall rotation note: Chris taking lead at 13:15 UTC. Will post 15-min updates.

Avery: quick post-incident actions (short):
- rollback quantization profile for canary (done)
- runtime toggle applied to streaming endpoints (temporary)
- scale up streamer pool (in effect)
- reproduce and patch dequant path as async (Diego)
- run extended canary tests for long-context workloads (Rina)
- follow-up postmortem and action items doc (Avery)

Rina: I'll add a preflight test to the calibration rollout pipeline to simulate KV patterns and streaming. Should prevent this in future.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to MONITORING state. Severity downgraded to P2 pending repro/patch.

Avery: final note before handoff — timeline, customer impact, mitigation steps and links will be put into the incident ticket: https://incidents.redwood/ISSUE-2026-1297. Handoff complete.

Chris: taking over monitoring. If we see p99 > 500ms above baseline again, I will throttle canary traffic and call for immediate reopen.

Maya: thanks team. I'll prepare the postmortem draft and coordinate with CS for customer followups. :thumbsup:

Lia: support ticket updates posted. customers acknowledged and appreciated fast response.

Diego: will drop repro PR and initial async dequant prototype by EOD.

Avery: closing active paging thread, updating incident ticket. Good catch everyone.
